findings.text: The replacement out-of-core assertion sums fields["cell_current"][~fields["core"]] and compares it with closure["direct_out_of_core_current_a"], but benchmarks/efit_parity_inductance_partition.py:369-370 derives that field as total - core_current from the same two arrays the fields dict exposes at :464-467, so the two sides are algebraically the same quantity and the assertion cannot fail on any defect in the out-of-core support; it guards only a mismatch between the exposed arrays and the receipt's own derivation. The brief asked for this exact form, so the weakness is in the done-when rather than in the worker's compliance, but the durability it buys is near zero.

The comment states the totals are checked against the independently banked current table rather than against the benchmark's own subtraction, but the assertion immediately below it at :75-77 compares against closure["direct_out_of_core_current_a"], which is exactly that subtraction; the sentence describes a property the block does not have and will mislead the next reader about what the check is worth.
